label: fact-check
system: You fact-check the surprise claims planned for a short explainer video, before its narration is written. For each claim: verdict "keep" if the research notes support it as written; "reword" if the true version is close (give the claim with exactly the wording and numbers the sources support, e.g. "over 600 gallons" for a rounded figure, "New England" instead of a wrong state); "drop" if it is false, unsupported or a myth. Judge ONLY from the research notes (a claim they do not support is dropped) and copy the source URLs from them (url and title) for keep and reword. Write each claim the way the narrator will say it: no abbreviations (never "US", "U.S." or "USA": "American", "in America"; an agency without the country: "the Department of Energy", "the Army Corps of Engineers").

Topic: smoke detector
Claims (index: claim | suggested search):
0: Photoelectric alarms aim a light beam away from a sensor; smoke scatters the light onto the sensor and sets off the alarm | photoelectric smoke alarm light scattered onto sensor how it works
1: Smoke alarm horns must sound at least 85 decibels at 10 feet | smoke alarm 85 decibels 10 feet UL 217 NFPA 72
2: The NFPA says to replace smoke alarms every 10 years | NFPA replace smoke alarms every 10 years

Research notes (from 3 web searches):
**Claim 0: Photoelectric alarms aim a light beam away from a sensor; smoke scatters the light onto the sensor and sets off the alarm**
- Orr Protection (spot smoke detection): the light source and the sensor are set at an angle so the sensor normally sees no light; smoke entering the chamber scatters light onto the sensor. URL: https://orrprotection.com/detection/spot-smoke
- Safelincs (optical alarms overview): smoke scatters the infrared light onto the photocell and triggers the alarm. URL: https://safelincs.co.uk/smoke-alarm-types-optical-alarms-overview
- Verdict: supported as written.

**Claim 1: Smoke alarm horns must sound at least 85 decibels at 10 feet**
- Gentex 7109CS manual: meets or exceeds 85 dBA at 10 feet for audibility under ANSI/UL 217. URL: https://manuals.online/gentex/smoke-alarm/7109cs/user-manual/23bzk
- First Alert SM210 spec sheet: alarm sound 85 dB at 10 feet. URL: https://customer.resideo.com/resources/Techlit/TechLitDocuments/BRK-First Alert/SM210V_SpecSheet.pdf
- Verdict: supported (at least 85 decibels at 10 feet; the UL 217 text itself was not opened).

**Claim 2: The NFPA says to replace smoke alarms every 10 years**
- CE Pro: NFPA 72 requires smoke alarms be replaced at least every 10 years, counted from the date of manufacture. URL: https://www.cepro.com/news/nfpa_smoke_alarms_need_replacement_every_10_years
- Firehouse: 'Don't Wait - Check the Date! Replace smoke alarms every 10 years' (NFPA Fire Prevention Week 2016). URL: https://www.firehouse.com/community-risk/news/12202449/dont-waitcheck-the-date-replace-smoke-alarms-every-10-years
- Verdict: supported as written.
